This patient has been diagnosed with glioblastoma multiforme (GBM) involving the right hemisphere. The MRI scan shows an infiltrative lesion occupying most of the cerebral cortex bilaterally. The tumor appears well-defined but extends into adjacent white matter structures. There is no evidence of hemorrhage or cyst formation within the tumor itself.

Clinical Presentation
There were no symptoms suggestive of neurological deficit prior to surgery. However, postoperative evaluation revealed mild motor weakness on the left side which improved over time. No other significant complications have occurred during follow-up. 

Histopathology Analysis
Microscopic examination showed GBM cells invading through the pial surface and extending deep into the subcortical gray matter. The neoplastic cells had high nuclear-to-cytoplasmic ratio and prominent nucleoli. Immunohistochemistry staining demonstrated positive expression of synaptophysin and GFAP, while negative for CD10 and EMA. These findings support the diagnosis of GBM.

Treatment Plan
Based on these histologic features, we recommend upfront radiation therapy followed by debulking surgery. We will also consider adjuvant chemotherapy after surgery depending upon the response to radiotherapy. The goal is to achieve complete resection without compromising functional integrity. 

MRI Follow-Up
We plan to perform regular MRIs every three months following surgery to monitor for any signs of recurrence. If there's progression detected, additional treatments such as radiosurgery or chemoradiation could be considered. 

Literature Review
Several studies have shown promising outcomes using combined therapies like surgery plus RT/chemo/RFA. Additionally, some cases have benefited from pre-operative embolization before surgery.
